solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bank donation about to expire

indicators.note: about means the donation word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a donation of money is a grant
to expire is to die

explanation.surface: A charitable donation from a bank is about to lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the financial institution, but here it is a slope of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth is a slope, and a slope has an incline or gradient.

clue.text: A tiny stone in one could be a sign

parts.note: a gem is a small precious stone
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A small pebble inside something might be taken as an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Unfortunately a king gets overturned in this state

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Sadly, a monarch is toppled within some state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets overturned' turns A and K into KA after ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'this state' points to a US state, the largest one in the union.

clue.text: Practise deception — not well, and due to be replaced

parts.note: someone not well is ill

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of due are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Faking sickness so a debt can be deferred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' rearranges DUE into UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To illude is an old verb meaning to trick or delude, so it means practising deception.

clue.text: Koreans pry outrageously, just like he does!

definitions.text: Koreans pry outrageously, just like he does!

indicators.note: outrageously says the letters of the two words are wildly scrambled

explanation.surface: Some people snoop shamelessly, as a certain busybody would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges KOREANSPRY; the whole clue also describes the answer, who pries.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody who meddles in others' affairs is exactly one who pries, as the clue says.

clue.text: Cold? I could make a hot meal

parts.note: a chill is a cold, the illness

explanation.surface: Feeling cold, someone thinks of cooking something warming.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy dish of beans and mince, commonly just called by its first word.

clue.text: Stolen property? [something that is] X-rated, apparently

parts.note: stolen goods are slang hot
stuff is one's possessions or property

explanation.surface: Is this stolen gear, or something only for adults?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for sexually exciting material, the kind given an adult film rating.

clue.text: House with joint title

parts.note: the House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A building and its owner share a single name or deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lords is Britain's upper parliamentary chamber, often just called the House.
explanation.definitionFit: His Lordship is a form of address used as a title for a peer or judge.

clue.text: I am Bill, the charlatan

parts.note: contracted as I'm
a bill is a printed notice, a poster

explanation.surface: A man named Bill confesses to being a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a placard.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan pretends to be someone or something they are not, like an impostor.

clue.text: Take some time at lessons like Friday, perhaps

indicators.note: take some means only a part of the following words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Spend a while at classes, as one might at the end of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: Many Christians traditionally avoid flesh on Fridays, eating fish instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday is traditionally a day without flesh for Catholics, so it is free of animal food.

clue.text: Purist is out to cause trouble

indicators.note: out means the letters of purist are put out of order

explanation.surface: A purist has left the room in order to make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate or provoke unrest is a phrasal verb meaning to cause trouble.

clue.text: Man as defined by primatologist, say

definitions.text: Man as defined by primatologist, say

parts.words: Man as defined by primatologist, say
parts.note: the zoologist Desmond Morris titled his book on humans with this phrase, a hairless primate

explanation.surface: How a scientist who studies apes would describe humankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Morris's 1967 book describes humans as a hairless primate, using this phrase as its title.

clue.text: Assist in motion? On the contrary!

indicators.note: in motion says the letters of assist move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Should one help something to move? No, quite the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' rearranges ASSIST; 'On the contrary' defines the opposite of motion, a standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: The contrary of being in motion is a standstill, a state of no movement.

clue.text: Innkeeper about to start the party

indicators.note: to start means the about piece comes at the front

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
a publican keeps a pub or inn

explanation.surface: A landlord is about to kick off the celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a celebration; it is the US political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are one of the two main political parties in the United States.

clue.text: From which 11 can trace his descent

definitions.text: From which 11 can trace his descent

parts.words: From which 11 can trace his descent
parts.note: 11 is the hairless primate, man; evolution is drawn as a branching diagram of all living things

explanation.surface: Where humankind's ancestry can be followed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The family tree here is the evolutionary diagram of all species, or the biblical tree in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The evolutionary chart of all living species is pictured as a branching tree, tracing man's ancestry.

clue.text: Begin the Ashes, possibly, with a fine performance

parts.note: to begin is to start
the Ashes is the cricket trophy between England and Australia, a small urn

explanation.surface: Opening a cricket series against Australia with a superb display.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes, the England-Australia cricket series, is played for a tiny urn; 'possibly' allows any urn of ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act of a show is its best performer or performance, hence a fine performance.

clue.text: Unresolvable photo finish?

parts.note: a race where even the camera at the line cannot separate the leaders

explanation.surface: A race result so close even the camera cannot decide.
explanation.definitionFit: When competitors cross the line together and no winner can be named, the race is tied.

clue.text: Mascara's blended with a kind of hair oil

indicators.note: blended means the letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: the s of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Make-up mixed together with some hair product.
explanation.definitionFit: Macassar oil was a Victorian hair dressing, which is why chairs had antimacassars.

clue.text: Beaters have done their job so there's no point going on

definitions.meaning: beaters on a shoot drive the birds, the quarry, up into the air

definitions.text: so there's no point going on
definitions.meaning: an idiom said when a scheme has been exposed or has failed

explanation.surface: The work is done, so we might as well give up.
explanation.walkthrough: On a shoot, beaters flush birds into the air for the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the deception is uncovered, or all is lost, while literally the quarry is flushed out.

clue.text: Criticise a sketch initially on canvas

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of sketch is used

parts.note: a sail is made of canvas

explanation.surface: Pan a drawing that was first done on artist's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them, including verbally, by harsh criticism.

clue.text: An incidental hit for a love child, once

parts.note: by- as in by-product or byway means incidental or secondary
a blow is a hit

explanation.surface: A chance knock and an illegitimate offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for an illegitimate child, hence 'once' for its old-fashioned use.

clue.text: Messenger wearing fewer clothes, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: wearing fewer clothes, you are more bare, barer

explanation.surface: A courier turns up wearing less than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: One who carries a letter or message to someone is its carrier or messenger.

clue.text: Like a starburst explosion the gunners face

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
the face of a clock is its dial

explanation.surface: Artillerymen confront an explosion that spreads outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' is a link word here, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A starburst has lines spreading out from a centre, so its pattern is radiating like spokes.

clue.text: Roman calendar that's out-of-date

definitions.meaning: the Julian calendar from Julius Caesar's Rome, replaced by the Gregorian one

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman way of dating that is now obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates by the old Julian calendar are so termed, and the phrase also means old-fashioned.

clue.text: Jumpy as a crowned head, proverbially

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's line from Henry IV says the head that wears a crown lies this way

explanation.surface: Nervous, as kings are said to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy means anxious, and Shakespeare's proverbial line says a crowned head lies in that state.

clue.text: Society sycophant who's a terrible writer

parts.note: a crawler fawns on superiors

explanation.surface: A fawning socialite who also happens to be a bad author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' means a person with bad handwriting, not a bad author.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy handwriting, so one who scrawls is a poor penman.

clue.text: Mother Earth, name only half true, oddly

indicators.note: only half means the first two of the four letters of name are kept
oddly means the letters of true are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: A name for the Earth goddess is only partly accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes NA from NAME; 'oddly' rearranges TRUE into TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Nature is the personification of the natural world, much like Mother Earth.

clue.text: Out of stock, for example

parts.note: stock is a garden plant; when it is out, it is blooming

explanation.surface: A shop label saying the goods have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of stock' reads as sold out, but stock is a flowering plant, and a plant that is out is blooming.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is out has its blooms open, which is the same as blossoming.
